maya: FYI seeing a sharp uptick in prefix cache miss rate after last night's rollout, stepping from ~12% -> ~43% for /chat-gen route :confused:
ajay: ugh. same window as the system prompt tweak? which change landed exactly?
maya: we pushed the system_prompt v2 that reorders tool params (made them alphabetical), + small serializer change in runtime-cache keying. deployment id: deploy/2026-03-17_23:02 by @nikki
liu: can you paste the cache logs? curious whether the key hash changed or if tokenization produced different byte sequences.
maya: pasting tail of cache debug (stripped):
```
CACHE_LOOKUP route=/chat-gen model=gptx-8k key_hash=0x9f1a3c miss
CACHE_LOOKUP route=/chat-gen model=gptx-8k key_hash=0xa7b2d1 miss
CACHE_STORE route=/chat-gen model=gptx-8k key_hash=0x3f12aa store_len=64
CACHE_LOOKUP route=/chat-gen model=gptx-8k key_hash=0x9f1a3c miss
```
maya: note many consecutive misses for similar prompts where previously we'd get hits.
nikki: I ran a local diff between the pre/post keying code — the canonicalization now preserves field order in the JSON toolcall string instead of normalizing to tuple list. that would definitely change keys. I thought alphabetical ordering would reduce churn but code path differs from the canonicalizer used in warmup tool.
ajay: oh — the warmup generator (prefix-warmup) still emits unordered tool args (dict iteration). So even though we changed canonicalization to alphabetical at runtime, our warmup entries don't match -> misses.
liu: another wrinkle: kernel selection uses recent sequence-length histograms to pick optimized attention kernels. If misses increase, we see shorter batching windows (less KV reuse) which flips kernel choice toward the latency-optimized path; that can cascade into higher p50 and p95. Checking perf traces now.
maya: perf traces attached from 23:10 window: 
```
TRACE: request_id=abc123 cache_hit=false batching_group=small kernel=latency-vec-1 p50=34ms p95=120ms
TRACE: request_id=abc124 cache_hit=true batching_group=large kernel=througput-vec-4 p50=12ms p95=44ms
```
nikki: so two separate effects: key mismatch -> miss rate -> smaller batches -> different kernel -> worse tail latencies. we need to decide whether to revert the canonicalization change or update warmup generator and warmup corpus to match.
ajay: quick mitigation: add temporary policy that treats toolcall field-order-insensitive when building cache keys (e.g., sort keys at probe time). That avoids changing warmup. Cheap guard.
liu: sorting at probe time duplicates work but cheaper than rollback. However watch out: sorted serialization must be stable across tokenizer versions. we already saw tokenizer pinning causing subtle hash deltas in past.
maya: can we roll that policy patch to canary (10% traffic) in the next 20m? deploy-bot: scheduled canary deploy: deploy/2026-03-18_00:10 -> canary=10% if all checks pass.
nikki: also will update prefix-warmup generator to emit sorted tool arg lists and re-run warmup job overnight.
ajay: add a regression test in eng-runtime tests: take sample toolcall permutations and ensure cache key equality after canonicalization. also add fuzzing to detect tokenizer-version sensitivity.
liu: I'll add a lightweight kernel-impact alert: if cache miss rate delta >15% AND median batch size decreases by >25% within 10m, alert eng-runtime-oncall.
maya: thanks. plan of record: 1) push probe-time stable-sort patch to canary (10%) 2) update warmup generation to produce sorted payloads + rewarm 3) add unit tests and fuzzing 4) monitor kernel selection shift and rollback if tail latencies cross SLO.
nikki: timeline sounds good. tagging @ajay to own canary patch. tagging @liu to own monitoring rule. I'll drive warmup re-gen.
ajay: on it, will open PR in 10m.
maya: appreciate the fast turnaround :thumbsup: any other quick wins? maybe also log a compact key diff telemetry so we can see which fields differ most often between pre/post keys.
liu: good idea — adding key-field-delta histogram to runtime telemetry (counts deltas by field name). helps root-cause future changes.
maya: ok folks i'll watch canary and report back in this thread.
deploy-bot: deploy/2026-03-18_00:10 canary job started (10% traffic). checks: smoke ok.
